Assessment of BA.evidence_source: Tylka and Wood-Barcalow (2015b) developed a revision of the scale, the 10-item. Two studies have examined the factor structure of the BAS-2 outside the United States. Using exploratory factor analysis (EFA), Atari (2016) reported that a Persian translation of the BAS-2 had a one-dimensional factor structure in samples of female and male university students in Iran. Similarly, an earlier EFA study provided evidence for a one-dimensional model of a Cantonese translation in female and male university students in Hong Kong (Cronbach's ˛= .90–.91; Swami & Ng, 2015). In order to facilitate wider use of the BAS-2 in Chinese-speaking populations, we report on the translation and validation of a Standard Chinese version of the scale.

It then discusses the development of the revised 10-item BAS-2 and reviews two previous studies (Atari, 2016 in Iran; Swami & Ng, 2015 in Hong Kong) that examined the BAS-2's factor structure and construct validity in university students. The section concludes by outlining the current study's aim to translate and validate a Standard Chinese version of the BAS-2 for wider use in Chinese-speaking populations.
